newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: SOCCER-SPAIN OPEN YOUTH CHALLENGE ON WINNING NOTE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPAIN OPEN YOUTH CHALLENGE ON WINNING NOTE.

text.p: Spain launched their challenge for the world youth soccer championship with a 2-1 victory over a combative Japan side in goup D on Wednesday.
Goals from Francisco Farinos and Miguel Angulo in the 22nd and 55th minutes gave the Spaniards the three points which put them top of the group.
In another group D game, Costa Rica and Paraguay drew 1-1.
Japan fought resolutely after falling 2-0 behind, cutting the deficit after 66 minutes when Atsushi Yanagisawa converted a spot kick, and striving in vain for the equaliser.

"My plan was, in the second half, we would attack more and create more chances," Japanese coach Masakuni Yamamoto said. "But in the first half, Spain were very tough and we struggled to deal with them."
Spanish coach Inaki Saez said: "In the second half, Japan were very tough. But before the game I had told my players that the first game is very important and all 18 of my players are very strong."
Pablo Chincilla scored Costa Rica's solitary goal in the 45th minute while Raul Roman replied for Paraguay in the 58th.
In group F, Mexico hammered the United Arab Emirates (UAE) 5-0, the biggest goal tally in the tournament so far.
